transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we go any further with this migration plan. During a compatibility rehearsal this morning, I confirmed that exactly 9 of our legacy pipelines cannot read artifacts from the new object-store path immediately. They require dual-writing to both stores for exactly 14 days before the final switch. I found this while helping another team validate its pipeline, and I haven't updated the migration proposal yet. This directly impacts the direct cutover approach in the current draft.

transcript.text: Thanks for flagging this, Ravi. This is a significant finding. A direct cutover would break those 9 legacy pipelines, so the current draft's approach won't work as-is. Before I can approve any migration plan, the release-readiness checklist requires both compatibility coverage and monthly cost controls to be confirmed. Right now, compatibility coverage is clearly not met with a direct cutover. We need to revise the proposal to include the 14-day dual-write period for those 9 pipelines. I'd also like to hear from anyone who can speak to the monthly cost controls piece — the current draft has no dedicated monthly cost alert, and that's another checklist item I need addressed before approval. Let's get the proposal updated and re-reviewed before next Wednesday's window.

I just reviewed the latest provider invoice minutes ago and confirmed that the projected egress pattern means this migration will exceed our team's approved spend once monthly storage and transfer costs reach $9,000. Because of that, the plan requires artifact retention of exactly 30 days — not the 90 days in the current draft — and a dedicated monthly cost alert set at exactly $9,000. I haven't filed the FinOps note yet, but this threshold is confirmed. So the current draft's 90-day retention and lack of a monthly alert both need to be corrected before this plan can meet the release-readiness checklist.
